target_customer: Web3 developers, music and NFT creators, later apps and institutions needing cross-chain execution
problem: Creators and apps found it hard to build token-based projects and let users transact across chains in one step.
business_model: Usage-based developer APIs and protocol fees

founders.name: Alexander Carlson
founders.background_notes: Music producer and singer per YC bio.

technical_complexity.rationale: Smart contract tooling and later cross-chain routing across many networks were hard but built on existing bridges and DEXs.

defensibility.rationale: Cross-chain routing was crowded with funded bridges and aggregators, and NFT tooling had low switching costs.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed it; MoonPay acquired it in May 2026 to power MoonPay Trade.

market_need_then: NFT and music NFT creators in 2021 and 2022 wanted no-code token tooling; the later cross-chain focus responded to fragmentation across chains.

branding.name_origin: Co-founder Will Collier said the name is a play on being the decent company for artists, bringing decency to an industry with indecent actors.
branding.domain_note: Uses decent.xyz, which now redirects to swaps.xyz.
branding.community_and_virality: Music world tie via investor Kygo; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly name but generic and shared with Decent DAO; the music angle faded after the pivot to infrastructure.

pivots.from: Music NFT and token-based project tooling for artists
pivots.to: Chain-abstracted UX and cross-chain routing APIs
pivots.why: Reported by The Block as a shift from music NFTs to cross-chain liquidity; no reason stated.

outcome_analysis: Decent started in 2021 as music and NFT infrastructure, raised a $3.5M Archetype-led seed in December 2022, then pivoted into cross-chain routing and chain abstraction APIs as NFT demand cooled. MoonPay acquired it in May 2026 to power an institutional trading platform across 200 plus chains, reportedly in a high eight-figure deal that MoonPay has not confirmed. The pivot to infrastructure created the buyer interest.
notes: Price reports of about $80M to $90M and high eight figures are unverified estimates; amount left null. CB Insights shows $4M over three rounds including an earlier convertible note, not recorded. Round date 2022-12-15 or 16 depending on source. The competitor search returned undated material, so the list is empty. Founder list per YC page includes four founders; some sources name only Durbin and Collier as co-founders.
